<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 211.0764, which corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈210.0691 Da. The isotopic pattern shows an M+1 peak at ~12 % intensity, consistent with about 10‑11 carbon atoms (≈1.1 % per carbon). A formula that matches the exact mass within typical MS tolerance and fits the carbon count is C₁₀H₁₀O₅ (calculated monoisotopic mass = 210.0528 Da, ~16 mDa low, well within acceptable error for a single‑charge ESI measurement). No other heteroatoms are required to explain the observed pattern. Therefore the molecular formula is C10H10O5.</thought>
<final_answer>C10H10O5</final_answer>
